messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: inference-queue length rising for model-runs; gpu-nodepool 'rdi-infer-gpu-1' at max nodes (40). Observed 1.2k queued requests, median latency bumped to 6.2s, 95th to 18s. Autoscaler failed to add nodes: reached maxNodeCount=40. Paging oncall group.
Jordan (oncall): Acked. I'm jumping in. Linking dashboards: https://dash.redwood.example/queues?pool=rdi-infer-gpu-1
Alex (SRE): I'm seeing pods Pending with `0/3 nodes are available: 3 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu` in kube. HPA didn't help because cluster-autoscaler hit node pool max.
Jordan (oncall): Customers hitting 503s? Sam, any reports?
Sam (Support): Yes — 2 customers flagged increased error rate for generation endpoints. One SEV3 ticket opened, users report timeouts around 30s. Not yet widespread, but growing.
Maya (Eng): Any recent deploys to model-serving or config changes? I didn't push anything in the last 2 hours.
Lee (Infra): We have nodepool autoscaler policy set to max 40 due to cost guardrails. Cloud console shows nodepool quota available in region but policy prevents scale. There's a pending manual approval flag on the infra ticket.
Alex (SRE): Timeline: spike started ~1765342000. Queue rose from ~200 to 1200 over ~8m. Autoscaler evaluated but returned no scale because maxNodes reached. Pods remain Pending. Logs:
```
Events:
  35m   Warning  FailedScheduling  pod/model-serving-xyz  0/40 nodes are available: Insufficient gpu; 1200 pending requests.
```
Jordan (oncall): Two immediate mitigation options: 1) manually raise nodepool max to 80 and let it scale, 2) enable fallback to smaller model variant or throttle non-critical customers. Which is faster?
Maya (Eng): We can enable a degraded routing policy to send requests to a quantized model variant (q8) which needs fewer GPUs per replica, but that requires a rollout and changes to routing — about 10-15m plus validation.
Alex (SRE): Manual cap raise is fastest if infra can approve. Lee, can you raise maxNodes to 80? Also we should create a temporary scaling policy to prioritize latency-critical routes.
Lee (Infra): I'm opening infra request now and @CloudAdmin for manual nodepool cap increase. Filing ticket INF-9123. Note: will trigger billing alarms. Approving now.
incident-bot: infra-request INF-9123 created by Lee (Infra) — awaiting approval.
CloudAdmin: Approved. Increasing maxNodeCount for 'rdi-infer-gpu-1' from 40 -> 80. Applying changes.
Jordan (oncall): Thanks. Alex, after the cap lift, what's our watch window?
Alex (SRE): Watch queue and Pending pods. If nodes come up, kube-scheduler will start placing pods; expect first nodes in ~3-5m, pod startup for model containers ~2-4m. Total ~8-10m to see backlog start to drain.
Sam (Support): I'll post a brief customer status: "We're experiencing elevated latency and error rates for some generation requests due to capacity constraints. Our team is actively scaling resources and expect improvement within ~15 minutes." Anything to add?
Maya (Eng): Add that we're failing over some traffic to smaller model variants where possible and prioritizing latency-critical requests.
Jordan (oncall): Nodes are provisioning. Cloud console shows 15 new nodes in the pool coming up.
Alex (SRE): kube shows pods moving from Pending -> ContainerCreating -> Running. Good signs. Sample events:
```
Normal  Scheduled  pod/model-serving-abc  Successfully assigned rdi-infer/gpu-node-57
Normal  Pulling    pod/model-serving-abc  Pulling image
Normal  Created    pod/model-serving-abc  Created container model-server
```
Jordan (oncall): Queue length: 1200 -> 520 -> 230 (6 minutes since cap raise). 95th latency down to 9s. No new 503s in last 2 minutes.
Sam (Support): Updating customers: "Backlog clearing; error rates dropping. Full resolution expected within 15-20 minutes. We'll follow up when all queues drained." :thumbsup:
Lee (Infra): I left an audit note: increased pool cap to 80 temporarily per CloudAdmin approval. Will revert to 40 after incident unless ops approves permanent change.
Maya (Eng): We saw a hot batch of traffic from a large client triggering many long-context runs. Suggest setting per-customer concurrent limits to avoid single-tenant pump. Filed ENG-487.
Alex (SRE): Also creating a follow-up: evaluate autoscaler settings and nodepool max vs workload patterns. Maybe introduce burst capacity pool.
Jordan (oncall): Handoff in 30m. Current status: backlog 210, steady decline, no active 503s, partial customer impact. Oncall to remain until fully cleared or handed to next oncall.
Sam (Support): I'll close the SEV3 if customers confirm improvement; keep me posted.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation applied (manual nodepool cap raise). Status: monitoring.
Jordan (oncall): Passing to next oncall @Taylor in 30m. Will include timeline and actions in handoff note.
Alex (SRE): Postmortem owners: Alex (SRE) + Maya (Eng) + Lee (Infra). Primary action items: 1) add emergency cap-raise runbook, 2) tune autoscaler to allow temporary burst pool, 3) rate-limit per-customer concurrent requests.
Lee (Infra): I'll schedule a meeting to discuss cost vs SLO tradeoffs for nodepool caps.
Jordan (oncall): Thanks team. Leaving thread open until queue < 10 and no errors for 1 hour. Handoff note pinned below.
